title: What Happens If You Fall Into a Black Hole?
credits: Footage: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center / Jeremy Schnittman, NASA Scientific Visualization Studio

scenes.text: What would happen if you fell into a black hole? NASA ran a supercomputer simulation to find out. And the answer... is terrifying.
A black hole forms when a giant star collapses on itself. Its gravity becomes so strong that nothing can escape. Not even light.
scenes.fact: If Earth were crushed into a black hole,\Nit would be about the size of a marble.

scenes.caption: THE BLACK HOLE AT THE CENTER OF OUR GALAXY
scenes.text: And at the center of our own galaxy sits one as heavy as four million suns.
That glowing ring is gas, spinning at a huge fraction of the speed of light. Gravity bends its light so much, we can even see the back of the disk, above and below.
label: ACCRETION DISK
LIGHT BENT BY GRAVITY

scenes.heading: SPAGHETTIFICATION
scenes.text: As you fall, gravity pulls on your feet much harder than on your head. Your body gets stretched... like spaghetti. Scientists actually call it spaghettification.
In NASA's simulation, once you cross the event horizon, you have just twelve point eight seconds before being torn apart.
label: EVENT HORIZON
THE POINT OF NO RETURN
scenes.fact: Near a black hole, time slows down. From far away,\Nyou would seem to freeze at the edge forever.

scenes.caption: FROM THE EVENT HORIZON TO SPAGHETTI

scenes.text: And black holes don't stay quiet. In twenty twenty-five, astronomers caught what may be a black hole devouring a star, producing the longest gamma-ray burst ever seen.
label: GRB 250702B
LONGEST GAMMA-RAY BURST EVER SEEN
scenes.yt_chapter: A Black Hole Eats a Star

scenes.text: So... would you take the trip? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe. The universe is stranger than you think.

What would really happen if you fell into a black hole? Using a NASA supercomputer simulation, we follow the fall step by step: the glowing accretion disk, spaghettification, the event horizon, and the 12.8 seconds that follow.

In this video:
• What a black hole really is
• Why we can see the back of the accretion disk
• Spaghettification explained
• Why time slows down near the event horizon
• The black hole that devoured a star in 2025
